subject.title: feat(slack): Support Slack RTS (Real-Time Search) API via assistant action tokens

question: Should OpenClaw add Slack RTS as a separate assistant action-token search path, and what exact token containment, authorization, and scope rules must it use?
rationale: The requested capability handles event-scoped Slack action tokens and workspace search results, so automation should not choose token retention, redaction, or workspace-search semantics without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve a narrow RTS contract
options.body: Implement `assistant.search.context` inside the Slack plugin with event-scoped action-token containment, read-target/privacy safeguards, docs, tests, and live Slack proof.

options.title: Consolidate Slack search first
options.body: Define one Slack search contract covering RTS and user-token `search.messages`, then implement only the approved path.

options.title: Defer workspace search
options.body: Keep Slack workspace search out of OpenClaw until maintainers are ready to own the token, privacy, scope, and proof burden.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow RTS contract
recommendation.body: Implement `assistant.search.context` inside the Slack plugin with event-scoped action-token containment, read-target/privacy safeguards, docs, tests, and live Slack proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest recent history across Slack assistant context, action runtime, docs, and the related broad Slack action-parity discussion.
